clue.text: Leaders of council here ashamed of such confusion

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: The heads of a town council are embarrassed by the muddle they have made.
explanation.definitionFit: Total disorder or turmoil is a synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Lords and ladies crazed by drink

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for mad or crazed
a pint is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: Aristocrats of both sexes driven wild by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' looks like the nobility but is the country name of the wild arum plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and ladies is a folk name for the wild arum, a woodland plant also called by this name.

clue.text: 25's origins giving rise to gossip

indicators.note: origins means only the opening letters of the other answer are kept, its remainder dropped

parts.note: the answer to 25 across is the word for relief from pain

explanation.surface: Some source gives birth to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' keeps only ANA, the start of ANALGESIA; 'giving rise to' joins wordplay to definition (and ANA would read the same upwards anyway).
explanation.definitionFit: Ana is a collection of anecdotes and table talk about a person, hence gossip.

clue.text: Son frequently exhibiting temper

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A boy who regularly loses his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like a noun for anger but is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or tone it down.

clue.text: Duplicity of tax every ruler introduced

indicators.note: introduced means these pieces are brought inside the first word

parts.note: to try is to strain or tax, as in trying someone's patience
each means every
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Every monarch's new levy was a betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal and double-dealing, the essence of duplicity.

clue.text: Work taken up by writer having no alternative?

definitions.text: Work taken up by writer having no alternative?

parts.words: Work taken up by writer having no alternative?
parts.note: a reference work that a writer picks up when stuck for another word, a book full of alternatives

explanation.surface: A book picked up by an author who has run out of options.
explanation.definitionFit: This reference book lists synonyms, so a writer lacking an alternative word consults it.

clue.text: Spooky English lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: An English lake with a haunted atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky and uncanny are synonyms describing something weird and frightening.

clue.text: It's easy to go round centre of Leeds — pedestrianised

indicators.note: to go round means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a pedestrianised street is car-free

indicators.note: centre of picks out the middle letter of the word Leeds

explanation.surface: Walking is easy around Leeds city centre now cars are banned.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR-FREE goes round E, the middle letter of Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and untroubled, free of worry, as in an easy manner.

clue.text: Modern technology used to reinterpret stone circle

indicators.note: reinterpreting means rearranging the letters of the two words into a new reading

explanation.surface: Archaeologists use up-to-date gadgets to study an ancient monument afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: The field of circuits and devices such as computers is a hallmark of modern technology.

clue.text: Toy — start off, and it repeatedly comes up

definitions.text: Toy — start off, and it repeatedly comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are read upwards
repeatedly means the remaining letters are written twice
start off means the first letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A plaything you set going that keeps rising again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' drops the T from Toy to leave OY; 'repeatedly' doubles it to OYOY and 'comes up' reverses that to YOYO.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning toy on a string that climbs back up to the hand again and again.

clue.text: At worst, a slave? driver?

parts.note: a person paid to drive others about might at worst be called a slave, or be thought of as a slave-driver

explanation.surface: A man employed to drive who feels little better than a slave.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the last two words together as 'slave-driver', then apart: the employee is a driver, and at worst a slave to the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to drive a car for someone else, a private driver.

clue.text: Delicate and slender maiden drops out of treatment

indicators.note: drops out of means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a remedy is a treatment for illness
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A frail thin girl gives up her course of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a reed: thin and tall, or of a voice, thin and high, so slender and delicate.

clue.text: Where you see card's pips, at first glance

definitions.meaning: the pips showing a playing card's value are printed on its front side

explanation.surface: A card player judges a hand by the symbols showing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means judging by appearances, and literally the pips are printed on a card's front.

clue.text: Exactly how rent should be paid

definitions.meaning: rent is paid to the landlord, the one who lets, playfully a letter

explanation.surface: A tenant pays rent precisely as agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter' here is one who lets property, so rent is paid to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Following instructions precisely, in every detail, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Sweet to eat that might improve the complexion

parts.note: afters is British slang for a dessert or sweet course
to have food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A dessert that is good for the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is everyday British for pudding, the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion applied to the face after a razor, soothing and freshening the skin.

clue.text: 23 stone — how fatty finishes up

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit

indicators.note: finishes points to the closing letter of the word fatty

explanation.surface: A heavy man wonders how he ended up so fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to the answer RUTH, an old word for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word meaning compassion or sorrow for another.

clue.text: Fed up after grilling?

definitions.meaning: food cooked under a grill is browned and then taken off

explanation.surface: Someone tired of being interrogated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grilling' suggests interrogation; here it is cooking, after which food is browned and lifted off.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for irritated or bored, fed up with something.

clue.text: Don't settle and dwell — it has strings attached

parts.note: to welsh is to avoid settling a debt
to harp on is to dwell on a subject

explanation.surface: A conditional deal you should neither accept nor brood over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' sounds like conditions; it is literally an instrument with strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple-strung harp traditional in Wales, an instrument fitted with strings.

clue.text: Waterfall interminably tumbling — it's all part of the service

definitions.text: it's all part of the service

indicators.note: tumbling means the remaining letters fall into a new order
interminably means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Endless cascades of water are all included in the tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' drops the final L of WATERFALL; 'tumbling' rearranges WATERFAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates and cutlery form a dinner service, the tableware set.

clue.text: Gratuitously provokes tinker

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke them
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A travelling mender stirs up trouble for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Without need or good reason, for no cause, which is what gratuitously means.

clue.text: Take wrong turning, get charged

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: evil is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A driver who goes the wrong way gets a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire carrying current is electrically charged.

clue.text: Minor cut, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them

explanation.surface: A small wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means small and trivial, and as a verb to snub or cut someone.

clue.text: Settler — he isn't disposed to engage in controversy

indicators.note: disposed means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A colonist who prefers not to argue.
explanation.definitionFit: To join a contest, from knights riding into the jousting arena; figuratively to enter a dispute.

clue.text: River — every bit of it

parts.note: each means every

explanation.surface: The whole length of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: R (river) plus EACH (every), and the whole clue describes a stretch of river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of a river between two bends or locks.

clue.text: Book revealing what actually occurred? Not the first time

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the truth is what really happened

explanation.surface: A book that reveals the facts once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Extreme and difficult race in which to take part

indicators.note: taking part in the words means a run of letters is drawn from inside them

explanation.surface: A gruelling event that athletes enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as a prefix or adjective means beyond the usual, extreme.

clue.text: Seal again, after treatment giving relief from pain

indicators.note: after treatment means the letters have been worked on and reordered

explanation.surface: Resealing a wound after medical care brings comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence of sensitivity to pain, the effect of painkillers.

clue.text: Clout, for example

explanation.surface: A punch, as an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a say means influence, and say also introduces an example.

clue.text: Nag parliamentarian to provide assistance for drivers

parts.note: a nag is a horse
a whip is an MP who enforces party discipline

explanation.surface: An MP harasses colleagues to help motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists; here they drive horses and coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A long whip used by those driving horses or coaches to urge them on.

clue.text: Shrub in which bird is heard

indicators.note: is heard means the word is said aloud and a word that sounds the same is written

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, from bird-lime rhyming with time

explanation.surface: A bush where a songbird can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like a feathered creature but is British slang for a spell in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A small aromatic shrubby herb of the mint family.
